name: Risk Factor Disclosure
description: Offering memoranda must contain a comprehensive Risk Factors section disclosing all material investment risks. This includes liquidity risk, market risk, manager dependence, valuation uncertainty, leverage risk, regulatory risk, and counterparty risk. Risk disclosures must be specific, not generic, and must caution investors about the potential loss of their entire investment.

name: Fee and Expense Disclosure
description: All management fees, performance / carried interest fees, transaction fees, organizational expenses, and placement fees must be fully disclosed, including offset mechanisms and clawback provisions. Fee offset and carried interest calculations must be verifiable by investors.

name: Investor Eligibility and Securities Act Compliance
description: Interests offered under Rule 506(b) of Regulation D may only be sold to accredited investors. Section 3(c)(7) fund exemptions require qualified purchaser status for all investors. The offering must comply with Section 4(a)(2) private placement exemption or Regulation D. No general solicitation or general advertising is permitted.

name: Conflicts of Interest Disclosure
description: Investment advisers must disclose all material actual and potential conflicts of interest, including co-investment policies, allocation policies, side letters, affiliate fees, and multi-fund management conflicts. Regulation S-K and Form ADV Part 2A require written disclosure of conflicts and how they are managed.

name: Distribution Waterfall and Clawback
description: Private fund offering documents must clearly describe the distribution waterfall including return of capital, preferred return / hurdle rate, general partner catch-up, and carried interest split. Clawback obligations must be disclosed including escrow arrangements and personal guarantee provisions.

name: Transfer Restrictions and Liquidity
description: Offering documents must clearly disclose restrictions on transfer, including consent requirements, absence of a secondary market, and lock-up periods. Investors must be warned that interests are illiquid and that no liquidity is expected for the full duration of the fund.

name: Key Person and Suspension Provisions
description: Where the fund's performance depends on specific individuals, offering documents should disclose key person provisions that trigger suspension of the investment period upon departure of named individuals and the process for reinstatement of the investment period.

name: Investor Reporting Obligations
description: Offering memoranda must disclose the frequency and content of financial reporting to investors, including quarterly reports and timelines, annual audited accounts and timelines, tax reporting obligations, and capital account statements.

name: Investment Restrictions and Concentration Limits
description: Private fund offering documents must clearly specify investment restrictions, concentration limits, geographic restrictions, leverage limits, and prohibited asset classes. Restrictions may only be amended with investor or advisory committee approval.

name: Valuation Policy and Fair Value
description: Investment advisers managing private funds are required under SEC guidance and Rule 2a-5 under the Investment Company Act to adopt written valuation policies. Valuations of illiquid assets must be performed by or with oversight of a qualified independent party at least annually.

name: Regulatory Compliance — Advisers Act and Investment Company Act
description: General partners and investment managers of private funds must disclose registration status under the Advisers Act, their compliance programme under Rule 206(4)-7, AML/KYC obligations under the Bank Secrecy Act, and OFAC sanctions compliance. Required recordkeeping under Rule 204-2 must be described.

name: ERISA Plan Asset Considerations in OM
description: Offering memoranda for private funds that may receive investment from ERISA-governed benefit plans must disclose the fund's benefit plan investor monitoring, the 25% threshold test, and the consequences of plan asset status for the fund manager.

name: AIFMD and Cross-Border Distribution
description: Funds marketed to EU investors must comply with the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Directive (AIFMD), including disclosure of remuneration, leverage, liquidity, annual report requirements under Article 22, and regulatory reporting under Articles 23–24.
